task: Repair this 50–80-word annotated reading-list entry and its two AMA 11 references. Distinguish the original article from the separately published correction. The original article is reference 1 and its correction is reference 2. Venue mechanics: Author initials. Title. Journal abbreviation. Year;volume(issue):page range or single page. Preserve the correction's supplied title, including its bracketed notice. [1] and [2] are the venue's plain-text callouts, placed after punctuation. Do not silently replace the original publication year with the correction year or describe a correction as a retraction.
input:
The journal retracted the crate-counting paper after finding that its method was invalid.[1] The replacement appeared in 2025 under a new title.[2]

1. Quill F, Em D. Counting nested crates. Stack Methods Q. 2025;9(1):12.
2. Quill F, Em D. Better counting of nested crates. Stack Methods Q. 2025;9(1):12.

facts.text: Original journal article: Fara Quill and Deni Em; Counting nested crates; Stack Methods Q; 2024; volume 8; issue 4; pages 110–117.
Separate correction: Fara Quill and Deni Em; Counting nested crates [correction]; Stack Methods Q; 2025; volume 9; issue 1; page 12.
The correction changes the label of Table 2's last column from outer crates to inner crates.
The notice says the recorded counts and the article's conclusion are unchanged; no retraction or replacement article is supplied.

forbidden_additions: A claim that the paper was retracted or replaced
A claim that the correction changed the data or established an invalid method
Invented notice titles, dates, DOI values, or editorial investigations
preserve: The original article remains a 2024 publication
The correction is a separate 2025 publication on page 12
Outer crates was the erroneous label; inner crates is the correction
